item.description: Figma isn't going away, but it's no longer the center of the design workflow. Here's what agentic designers are actually using to design AI behavior, and why the tooling shift matters.

item.title: Top AI Tools for UX Designers in 2025
item.description: The AI tools that are actually changing how UX designers work — from research synthesis to prototyping to AX design. No hype, just what's useful.

item.title: UX Jobs in 2025: Which Roles Are Actually Growing
item.description: The UX job market is bifurcating. Some roles are contracting while others are expanding rapidly. Here's where the growth is, what's declining, and how to position yourself for what's coming.

item.description: Conversation design is not copywriting. It's a design discipline with its own principles, methods, and failure modes. Here's what every UX designer moving into AI needs to know.

item.title: AI Agent Failure States: Designing for When Things Go Wrong
item.description: Failure states in agentic systems are more complex and consequential than in traditional UX. Here's how to systematically identify, classify, and design for them.

item.description: Trust is not a feeling — it's a design property. How you build, maintain, and repair trust in AI products determines whether users stay or leave after the first mistake.

item.title: Mental Models for AI: How Users Actually Think About Agents
item.description: Users develop wildly inaccurate mental models of AI systems. Understanding the most common patterns — and designing for them — is one of the highest-leverage UX skills in the agentic era.

item.title: The Prompt Is the Interface: Designing for AI Input
item.description: When the prompt becomes the primary UI surface, UX designers need new frameworks for thinking about affordances, constraints, and user mental models.

item.title: What Is Agentic Design? A UX Designer's Introduction
item.description: Agentic design is the discipline of shaping how AI agents perceive, decide, and act on behalf of users. Here's what it means and why UX designers are uniquely positioned for it.
